newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia to introduce cyber laws by March - minister.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia to introduce cyber laws by March - minister.

text.p: Malaysia is drafting five new "cyber laws" to underpin its ambition of becoming a global hub for multimedia firms, Energy, Telecommunications and Posts Minister Leo Moggie said on Monday.
"We will...be building the soft infrastructure -- the legislation. In the March sitting of Parliament, we will introduce five new pieces of legislation," Moggie said.
They are the Computer Criminal Act, the Digital Signature Act, amendments to the Copyright Act, the Telemedicine Act and the Electronic Government Act, he said.
Speaking to an electronic commerce conference in Kuala Lumpur, he said: "We are not constrained by existing laws and regulations, so we can leapfrog over other countries.
"No other country is doing this in such a comprehensive way. We are building the physical structure and the legal framework," Moggie said.

The Multimedia Super Corridor is a proposed 15 by 50 kilometre (nine by 30 mile) zone from Kuala Lumpur south to where a new international airport and futuristic federal capital are under construction.
Malaysia hopes to lure software companies, electronic publishers, internet providers, telemedicine and electronic education firms to invest there.

"The main thrust of the Digital Signature Act is to give certification and authority to certify agencies that recognise digital signatures. It is intended to make sure signatures are safe and secure. Such signatures will be deposited in a repository," Moggie told reporters after the opening ceremony.
The Digital Signature Act and the Computer Crime Act have already been drafted, while the Telemedicine Act and the Electronic Government Act are still being readied, he said.
